frozen_hypothesis.hypothesis: In the Morpholine–tBuBrettPhos target, 100 °C conditions using strong non-nucleophilic amidine bases should outperform the 30 °C and triethylamine options, with the most likely high-yield region centered on same-precatalyst-supported MTBD/DBU settings at moderate residence time and ~1.1–2.2 base equivalents.
frozen_hypothesis.mechanism: Transfer is grounded primarily in the same-precatalyst datasets, where tBuBrettPhos repeatedly shows its best outcomes under hotter conditions with strong organic bases, and where both short- and longer-residence successful regimes exist. Candidate 005 is the strongest source-supported anchor because it matches the common high-performing pattern for tBuBrettPhos: 100 °C, strong amidine base, moderate residence time, and moderate base equivalents. Candidate 002 tests whether the similarly source-supported DBU family is superior at comparable long residence time and slightly higher equivalents, consistent with excellent aniline+tBuBrettPhos performance. Candidate 010 preserves source-supported geometric coverage by probing the low-equivalent, very short-residence DBU regime that was also successful in aniline+tBuBrettPhos, helping distinguish whether morpholine follows a fast-turnover or longer-contact optimum while remaining inside the credible quality region.
failure_conditions: If morpholine behaves unlike the other amine-class substrates under tBuBrettPhos and instead prefers weaker or more nucleophilic bases, this hypothesis fails.
If the doubled precatalyst loading in the target changes the base-response landscape enough that source-local optima no longer transfer, the selected region may not be best.
If 30 °C candidates or triethylamine candidates outperform these 100 °C amidine-base selections, the central transfer claim is falsified.
If all three selected candidates give similarly poor yields, then same-precatalyst source similarity was not predictive for this target.
